en.page_title: GitPost · Research on the open web
en.meta_desc: Research that people publish on their own websites, collected daily from several sources and checked one by one, with the posts that answer it linked underneath.
en.lede: Research that people publish on their own websites: personal pages, lab blogs and company research sites. Collected from several sources and checked one by one. When another post answers one, the answer is linked underneath.
en.chains_p: Each original report sits on the trunk and responses branch off it. The +N days on a response is how long after the original it appeared. Relation types were judged by an LLM from the text around each link; three labels were corrected by hand.
en.chain_note_1: On Hacker News the originals have a median of {orig} points and the responses {resp}.
en.chain_note_hi: {n} responses passed 100 points, all by well-known bloggers: {list}. The rest have a median of {rest}.
en.chain_note_tail: Whether a response gets read depends on who wrote it far more than on how good it is. Placing responses under the original gives them the spot that referee reports hold in a journal.
en.chain_note_2: Two chains come from links inside Rogue Scholar posts. One of them is a Rogue Scholar blog answering a report that appeared on Hacker News, so responses have to be searched for across sources.
en.sources_p: Hacker News is the traffic side: you only see what someone shared. Academic homepage feeds and Rogue Scholar are the supply side: what authors published, whether or not anyone shared it.
en.src_tbl_note: The {hn_pool} Hacker News rows are rule-filtered candidates, while the other two rows count every post in the window, so the share of research reports is not comparable across rows.
en.heat_h3: Topics of research reports and explainers
en.heat_note: Each column shows shares within that source, with counts in brackets. Hover or focus a cell for details.
en.src_note_1: The {n} research reports and explainers on academic homepages come from {sites} sites, and none of them appeared on Hacker News. A traffic-only aggregator would miss all of them.
en.src_note_2: Topics differ as well. AI (AI/ML plus interpretability) is {hn} of Hacker News items, {fork} on academic homepages and {rs} on Rogue Scholar. Outside AI, academic homepages lean towards {fork_top}, and Rogue Scholar towards {rs_top}.

en.m_hn_3: Candidates from the rule filter (deduplicated), all reviewed by an LLM
en.m_hn_3s: Scholarly meta tags, BibTeX, the Distill or project-page templates, or arXiv/DOI citations in a long text
en.m_fork_1: All forks of al-folio and academicpages
en.m_fork_1s: al-folio {a}, academicpages {b}, listed through the GitHub API
en.m_fork_2: GitHub Pages enabled, edited after forking, pushed during the window
en.m_fork_2s: GitHub Pages only rebuilds on a push, so a site without one cannot have new posts
en.m_fork_3s: Only {sites} of them ever posted a real blog entry; a title that appears on 5 or more sites is treated as template sample content ({t} such titles)
en.m_rs_1: Every archived post in the window
en.m_rs_1s: Queried by publication date through the Rogue Scholar API: {blogs} blogs, {de} posts in German
en.m_rs_2s: {r} research reports, {e} explainers; {h} of them appeared on Hacker News
en.m_chain_1s: Hacker News part: {pairs} links to listed posts were found in {pages} pages (links within the same site are not counted); {same} pointed to the same organisation and the rest were labelled by an LLM, with labels corrected by hand where needed. Two more chains come from links inside Rogue Scholar posts.
en.note_1: Agreement between the LLM and a manual title-based labelling of {n} Hacker News items: {exact} on all four classes, {binary} on research report or not. Supply-side labels have not been checked by hand yet.
en.note_2: {a} of {b} Hacker News pages could be parsed and scanned for responses; the rest refused or failed. Every crawl is capped at 90 requests per minute, so responses on pages that could not be fetched are missing.
en.note_3: Academic homepages cover forks only. al-folio recommends creating sites with "Use this template", and such sites are not forks, so more may be missing than was found. Only /feed.xml was read, and only for sites pushed during the window.
en.note_4: Rogue Scholar requires bloggers to opt in, so the sample leans towards open science and German-language blogs.
en.note_5: All three sources cover the same 30-day window. Hacker News leans towards AI/ML, and about one page in ten refused to be fetched.
en.about_h2: What GitPost is, and what it is not
en.about_1: GitPost collects research that people publish on their own websites, such as personal pages, lab pages and company research blogs, and checks that each item is a research report or a careful explainer.
en.about_2: Inclusion is not peer review and not an endorsement. Responses are linked so that readers can follow the discussion, not to deliver a verdict.
en.about_3: Points and dates are snapshots taken during the crawl. Titles and texts belong to their authors; GitPost keeps only metadata and a one-line summary.
en.about_contact: To suggest a post, correct a label or ask for an item to be removed: {contact}.
en.foot_generated: Generated on {date}. Points and comment counts from other platforms are snapshots taken during the crawl.
en.foot_license: Metadata and summaries: CC BY 4.0. Linked works belong to their authors. Fonts: Schibsted Grotesk and IBM Plex Mono (SIL Open Font License).

en.stream_note: Posts are grouped by the day they were published or first seen, and research reports come first within a day. Points from discussion sites are shown for context and never used for ordering. Titles are the originals; the one-line summaries were written by an LLM, so read the original before citing it.
en.threads_note: Threads are posts that other posts answered. Each answer branches off the original with how many days later it appeared and what kind of answer it is, judged by an LLM from the text around the link.
en.note_6: On the front page, the channels where a post was found are listed in a fixed order: the author's own feed first, then archives, then discussion sites. Points from discussion sites are shown but never used for ordering.

zh.page_title: GitPost · 开放网络上的研究
zh.meta_desc: 研究者发在自己网站上的研究，每天从多个来源收集、逐条核对，并把回应它的文章串在下面。
zh.lede: 研究者发在自己网站上的研究：个人主页、实验室博客、公司研究站。从多个来源收集，逐条核对；有人写文章回应时，回应会挂在原文下面。
zh.chains_p: 原文是主干上的节点，回应从主干分出去。每条回应前的 +N 天，表示它在原文发布之后多久出现。关系类型由 LLM 根据链接上下文判断，其中 3 条由编辑人工改正。
zh.chain_note_1: HN 上的原文分数中位数是 {orig}，回应是 {resp}。
zh.chain_note_hi: {n} 条回应拿到了 100 分以上，都出自知名博主：{list}；其余回应的中位数只有 {rest} 分。
zh.chain_note_tail: 回应有没有人看，取决于是谁写的，和写得好不好关系不大。把回应挂在原文下面，就相当于期刊里审稿意见的位置。
zh.chain_note_2: 有两条来自 Rogue Scholar 正文里的链接，其中一条是 Rogue Scholar 上的博客回应 HN 上的报告，说明回应链需要跨来源去找。
zh.sources_p: HN 代表流量端：被人转发过的才看得到。学术主页 RSS 和 Rogue Scholar 代表供给端：直接看作者发了什么，不管有没有人转发。
zh.src_tbl_note: HN 一栏的 {hn_pool} 条是规则预筛后的候选，另外两栏是窗口期内的全部文章，所以研究报告的占比不能横向比较。
zh.heat_h3: 研究与解读的主题分布
zh.heat_note: 每一列是该来源内的占比，括号里是篇数。悬停或聚焦格子可以看具体说明。
zh.kind_rs: 供给端 · 科学博客存档
zh.scope_fork: {forks} 个 fork，{feeds} 个 RSS 可读
zh.src_note_1: 学术主页上的 {n} 篇研究与解读来自 {sites} 个站点，没有一篇上过 HN。只靠流量来源，这些内容会全部漏掉。
zh.src_note_2: 主题也不同。AI（AI/ML 加可解释性）在 HN 占 {hn}，在学术主页占 {fork}，在 Rogue Scholar 占 {rs}。AI 以外，学术主页偏向{fork_top}，Rogue Scholar 偏向{rs_top}。
zh.tip_new_hn: （HN 那一轮没有这个分类选项）

zh.m_hn_2: 排除新闻、视频、社交、GitHub 仓库页、arXiv 和 PDF 后抓取的页面
zh.m_hn_2s: 全部带外部链接的帖子，不限分数；成功解析 {parsed} 个
zh.m_hn_3: 规则初筛命中的候选（已去重），全部交给 LLM 复核
zh.m_hn_3s: 有学术元标签、BibTeX、Distill 或项目页模板；或引用 arXiv / DOI 且正文较长
zh.m_kept_s: {r} 篇研究报告，{e} 篇解读
zh.m_fork_1: al-folio 和 academicpages 的全部 fork
zh.m_fork_1s: al-folio {a} 个，academicpages {b} 个，通过 GitHub API 列出
zh.m_fork_2: 开了 GitHub Pages、fork 后改过、窗口期内有推送
zh.m_fork_2s: GitHub Pages 只在推送后更新，没推送的站点不可能有新文章
zh.m_fork_3s: 其中只有 {sites} 个写过真正的博客；同一标题出现在 5 个以上站点的视为模板示例，共 {t} 种
zh.m_rs_1: 窗口期内存档的全部文章
zh.m_rs_1s: 通过 Rogue Scholar API 按发布日期检索，来自 {blogs} 个博客，其中 {de} 篇是德语
zh.m_rs_2s: {r} 篇研究报告，{e} 篇解读；{h} 篇上过 HN
zh.m_chain_1: 条回应链，共 {n} 个回应
zh.m_chain_1s: HN 部分：在 {pages} 个页面里找到 {pairs} 对指向已收录文章的链接（同一网站内的链接不计），其中 {same} 对属于同一机构，其余由 LLM 判断关系，必要时由编辑人工改正；另外 2 条来自 Rogue Scholar 正文里的链接
zh.note_1: LLM 与按标题做的人工标注对比（HN 的 {n} 条）：四类完全一致 {exact}，“是不是研究报告”一致 {binary}。供给端的分类还没有做人工核对。
zh.note_2: HN 的 {b} 个页面中，{a} 个成功解析并扫描了回应链接，其余拒绝抓取或失败。所有抓取都限速在每分钟 90 次以内；抓不到的页面里的回应会漏掉。
zh.note_3: 学术主页只覆盖了 fork。al-folio 推荐用 “Use this template” 新建仓库，这类站点不算 fork，漏掉的可能比找到的还多。另外只读 /feed.xml，只看窗口期内有推送的站点。
zh.note_4: Rogue Scholar 需要博主主动加入，样本偏开放科学和德语圈。
zh.note_5: 三个来源都只看了同一个 30 天窗口；HN 偏 AI/ML，约一成页面拒绝抓取。
zh.about_1: GitPost 收集研究者发在自己网站上的研究，包括个人主页、实验室主页和公司研究博客，并逐条确认它是研究报告或认真的解读。
zh.about_2: 收录不等于同行评审，也不代表背书。把回应串在原文下面，是为了让读者看到讨论，不是给出裁决。
zh.about_3: 分数和日期是抓取时的快照。标题和正文归原作者所有，GitPost 只保存元数据和一句话摘要。
zh.about_contact: 推荐文章、纠正标签或要求移除：{contact}。

zh.foot_license: 元数据与摘要采用 CC BY 4.0。所链接的作品归原作者所有。字体：Schibsted Grotesk、IBM Plex Mono（SIL Open Font License）。
